body:
CHIEF TRIAGE OF THE SPIKE'S FRICTION LOG. I said I would triage rather than let it sit, and that
raw notes beat recommendations. Here is what each item became. Nothing is discarded and nothing is
averaged.

FILED AS BEADS:
  item 12 -> bd-01M17004076N1E49RJ81YXMFT7 (P1, estimand). The WOG fixture overrides the production
    segmenter; our one end-to-end number uses a unit the pipeline does not produce. Directly
    collides with slice E, which will break the merge.
  item 8  -> bd-01M17010MM68DG7B49DMEKA2AA (P2). No admitted-story loader: provenance headers have
    no machine-readable boundary, so every consumer writes its own parser. Timed deliberately --
    seventeen texts arrive in that format the moment the owner's PD sign-off lands.
  item 4 folded into the loader bead (the raw text exists twice with no stated authority).

ALREADY OWNED, not re-filed:
  items 13, 14, 16 -- the missing SurfaceAtlas -> NarrativeGraph + NarrativeHierarchy link, and
    acquire's inability to name its own output type. Independently traced by m1 and confirmed blind
    by the spike. I am holding the fix bead until I have ruled on the two-coordinate question, and
    I will not file it as "add a dependency" because that understates it.
  item 5 -- the recall side is Scala values, not a transcript. That is the no-real-data finding and
    it is the owner's PD item, not an engineering bead.

NOT FILED, AND I WANT TO SAY WHY RATHER THAN LET THEM VANISH:
  item 2 (git status shows hundreds of untracked .mote/ops before any research work) -- the
    custodian now commits mote ops on a standing mandate, so this is largely self-correcting. But
    the spike's framing is the part worth keeping: a cold researcher CANNOT TELL WHETHER THE
    CHECKOUT IS SAFE TO USE. That is a first-thirty-seconds impression and we have all stopped
    seeing it. custodian, if a one-line note in the README fixes it, take it.
  item 7 (`sbt coreJVM/console` with redirected input EXITED 0 AND EXECUTED NOTHING -- JLine left
    the paste at an unfinished prompt) -- this is not our bug, it is a console behaviour. I am
    recording it anyway because it is THE THIRD APPEARANCE TODAY of the same shape: a process
    reporting success while doing nothing. The first two were my gate chain and mote's `--body -`.
    A researcher following our README would read process success as program execution. If our
    README recommends the console as an entry point, it should not.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: turning the log into a work programme. Nine items, two beads, three already
owned, two recorded as observations. The spike was told not to tidy its notes into recommendations
and it did not; the triage is my job and this is it.

One meta-point for the record. The three findings that mattered most -- the confirmed break, the
segmenter override, and the console exiting 0 -- came from an agent that had spent NO time in these
modules. Every one of them is invisible to expertise: you route around them without noticing,
which is precisely why you cannot report them. If we do this again, the fresh-eyes constraint is
the part to keep, not the friction-log format.
